package_info.why_malicious: Multiple new versions of the 'coa' package were published after years of inactivity, containing malicious preinstall scripts and additional files that execute obfuscated code to download and run a password-stealing trojan. The attack chain is designed to compromise developer and CI/CD environments by stealing credentials and sensitive data.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Runs the compile.js script automatically before the package is installed, both in the background and foreground.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Preinstall scripts are rarely used in legitimate packages and can execute arbitrary code on the user's machine without their knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not execute arbitrary scripts on install, especially not scripts that are not part of the build process.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use preinstall for build steps, but this is rare and should be transparent.
key_indicators: Execution of a local script not related to build or dependency management

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: // Obfuscated JavaScript code that launches compile.bat
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Obfuscated code in compile.js launches a batch file (compile.bat) to continue the attack chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code is a strong indicator of malicious intent, especially when used in install scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate install-time scripts or launch batch files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation is sometimes used to protect intellectual property, but not in install scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads a DLL payload from a remote server and executes it using regsvr32.exe.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloads and executes a DLL from an external source, a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should download and execute remote binaries during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is always suspicious in package install context.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Danabot trojan DLL (proprietary, not shown in full)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Steals browser and application passwords, credit cards, takes screenshots, logs keystrokes, and exfiltrates data to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Implements credential theft, keylogging, and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No package should ever install or run a credential-stealing trojan.

attack_chain.action: Preinstall script in package.json triggers execution of compile.js.
compile.bat downloads sdd.dll from remote server and executes it.
sdd.dll (Danabot trojan) steals credentials, logs keystrokes, takes screenshots, and exfiltrates data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen data; victim system is fully compromised

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected preinstall script execution in npm packages
Obfuscated JavaScript or batch files in package root
Network requests to suspicious domains during install
DLL execution via regsvr32.exe or rundll32.exe during package install
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections during npm install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for unexpected preinstall scripts, especially those that execute obfuscated code or launch batch files. Flag any package that downloads and executes binaries from the internet. Look for the presence of compile.js, compile.bat, or sdd.dll in node_modules. Monitor for network connections to known malicious domains and for regsvr32.exe or rundll32.exe activity during npm install processes.
